incomplete_reasons: Section 232 duties other than those of U.S. note 16 (autos and parts, medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, timber and lumber, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals and others) and other chapter 99 duties whose U.S. notes define the goods by description, content or origin are not linked to commodity codes in this data set, so they may apply on top of these totals: check chapter 99 of the HTSUS (subchapter III) and CBP guidance

notes: The United States charges no import VAT; state sales or use tax may apply to the later sale or use of the goods.

Additional duties imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (HTSUS headings 9903.01 and 9903.02) are not applied: Executive Order 14389 of February 20, 2026 (91 FR 9437) says they "shall no longer be in effect and, as soon as practicable, shall no longer be collected". The Section 122 surcharge of headings 9903.03.01–9903.03.11 expired at the close of July 23, 2026 (HTS compiler's note).
The Section 301 additional duty on products of China (chapter 99, subchapter III, U.S. notes 20 and 31) does not apply when its condition document is presented (see the measure's conditions).

customs_value.rule: Transaction value: the price actually paid or payable for the merchandise when sold for exportation to the United States, plus packing, selling commissions, assists, royalties and license fees, and resale proceeds to the seller (19 CFR 152.103(b)); international freight and insurance are not part of it. Pass it in USD.

vat_value.rule: No import VAT: the United States levies no federal VAT or GST on imports.

fees.rule: Merchandise processing fee 0.3464% of the value of a formal entry (minimum $34.58, maximum $670.86), or $2.77 per automated informal entry (19 CFR 24.23; CBP Dec. 26-14); harbor maintenance fee 0.125% of the value of vessel cargo at listed ports (19 CFR 24.24).

disclaimer: An estimate from the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (USITC) as of the release date, not a ruling: U.S. Customs and Border Protection makes the final determination of classification, origin and duty. Section 232 duties are not included in the totals (the U.S. note 16 metal duties are listed with their conditions; the others are not linked), nor other chapter 99 duties defined by description, content or origin; check chapter 99, antidumping and countervailing duty orders and CBP guidance before you import.
